title: A minimal dynamical model of human-AI cognitive coevolution
abstract: arXiv:2611.06928v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The rapid deployment of generative AI raises the question of whether pervasive cognitive offloading drives a measurable, potentially irreversible decline in unassisted human reasoning. We examine this question with a phenomenological dynamical model based on the Cattell-Horn-Carroll distinction between fluid intelligence ($G_f$) and crystallized intelligence ($G_c$). Starting from the discrete-time Bivariate Latent Change Score formalism used in cognitive-aging research, we derive its continuous-time linear counterpart and introduce a fast third variable representing composite machine-intelligence capability. The machine variable enters the human subsystem through Hill-function modifications of the self-feedback and cross-coupling coefficients. translated_title: 人类-人工智能认知协同演化的最小动力学模型
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能的快速部署引发了一个问题：普遍的认知卸载是否会导致人类独立推理能力出现可测量的、潜在不可逆的衰退。我们基于卡特尔-霍恩-卡罗尔（Cattell-Horn-Carroll）理论中流体智力（$G_f$）与晶体智力（$G_c$）的区分，构建了一个唯象动力学模型来考察这一问题。从认知老化研究中使用的离散时间双变量潜在变化分数形式出发，我们推导出其连续时间线性对应形式，并引入一个表示综合机器智能能力的快速第三变量。该机器变量通过对自反馈和交叉耦合系数进行希尔函数修正而进入人类子系统。我们强调，该唯象模型同时捕捉了人工智能对人类认知的正面与负面影响。通过对正面和负面影响的定性概念进行形式化，w（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于流体智力与晶体智力区分的最小动力学模型，用于刻画生成式AI引发的认知卸载如何同时产生正面与负面影响，从而塑造人类认知与机器智能的协同演化。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a minimal dynamical model, built on the fluid-versus-crystallized intelligence distinction, that captures both the positive and negative effects of AI-driven cognitive offloading on human-AI cognitive coevolution.
